name: Blank Customer Problem Discovery Interview
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [industry persona] suffers from [critical operational bottleneck]. We will verify this by executing 15 structured problem interviews across 3 distinct sub-verticals, and consider it validated if ≥ 70% of interviewees rank this problem as one of their top two operational challenges for the current fiscal quarter.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Define the ideal customer profile from firmographic traits; frame outreach as research, not a sales pitch.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Ask for the quarter’s top three operational priorities and see whether the problem surfaces unprompted.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Score urgency one to five from documented budget, executive visibility and active software evaluations.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Define the Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) based on observable firmographic attributes. Secure interview access by framing outreach as academic or industrial research rather than commercial solicitation.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Introduce the macro domain and instruct respondents to identify their top 3 operational priorities for the quarter. Observe whether the hypothesized problem surfaces organically without prompting.

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Score the problem's organizational urgency on a 1–5 scale based on documented resource allocation, executive visibility, and active software evaluations.

warning.label: Polite Problem Inflation
warning.text: Interviewees lament minor inconveniences they have no budget or mandate to resolve.

warningFull: In professional contexts, interviewees frequently lament minor operational inconveniences that they have no budget or mandate to resolve.
